A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AGAV-Rater study. Their complete main texts, appendices, figures, tables, and equations support comparison, including matching renamed datasets and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original subjective ratings, model comparisons on AGAVQA/TTA/TTM, ablations, cross-dataset selection results, and an ElevenLabs user-preference experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds backbone comparisons, annotator-reliability analyses, and category-specific selection results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 3 retain the VideoLLaMA2 architecture, two-stage training, masking, and multidimensional score regression. The added loss and preprocessing descriptions document existing components. GroundingGPT and OneLLM are experimental alternatives, not replacements in the proposed method.

E1.justification: The training sources, AGAVQA-MOS/Pair, TTA/TTM benchmarks, and 230-video ElevenLabs study remain the same. AGAVQA becomes AGAVQA-3k without expanding coverage. Figure 2 revises source counts and removes a duplicated Kling label; its represented source types remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Random and MOS-fine-tuned AVID-CMA, VALOR, and VAST to the selection comparison, which previously compared against unfine-tuned LMMs. These alignment methods previously appeared in scoring experiments, so their participation here is new. Table 5 additionally compares GroundingGPT and OneLLM backbones.

E3.justification: The new backbone experiments fine-tune default weights with three-score regression heads, and the selection evaluation gains a trained-comparator arm. Existing cross-validation and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 introduces a 0–5 scoring description alongside retained 1–5 descriptions, leaving the annotation range inconsistent rather than establishing that ratings were recollected.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation with backbone ablations (Table 5), annotator agreement and relationships between scoring dimensions (Section 3.2 and Appendix B.5), and category-specific accuracy for the existing ElevenLabs study (Table 10). The original component ablations and MOS plots are retained.

E5.justification: v1 lacks quantitative annotator-reliability reporting. v2 adds Krippendorff's alpha, average correlations from ten random splits of subjects, and category-level inter-subject standard deviations (Section 3.2 and Table 7). The ten repetitions concern rating-consistency analysis, not additional model-training runs.

E6.justification: New results include selection accuracies of 0.52/0.55/0.64 for AVID-CMA/VALOR/VAST, backbone results, rating statistics, and category accuracies of 0.75–0.87. AGAV-Rater's selection accuracy remains 0.78, and all numerical cells in Tables 1, 2, and 4 are retained. Tables 1–2 correct the PLCC/KRCC headers, changing metric assignments rather than demonstrating performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1 is retained. Appendix C.2 supplies standard formulas for the cross-entropy and PLCC objectives already specified in v1; it does not introduce new theoretical reasoning, assumptions, proofs, or substantively different mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same dataset contribution, LMM-based multidimensional evaluator, leading benchmark performance, and improved user experience with 80% preference. The dataset rename and added Impact Statement do not materially alter these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for backbone performance and music pretraining, interpretations of rating variability, and the qualification that music aesthetics are not evaluated. Appendix B.5 also newly interprets SRCC 0.6860 as indicating independence between dimensions, an interpretation that the reported correlation does not establish.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed scoring rubrics, interface and equipment specifications, subject screening and fatigue controls, pretraining composition, loss formulas, audio preprocessing, training time, and direct code/dataset access information. These substantially improve documentation. However, the disclosed pretraining counts sum to 50,592, inconsistent with the stated 50,952 total.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GroundingGPT, OneLLM, Krippendorff reliability, and three Sun et al. papers on visual attention/perception. The principal related-work discussion and positioning relative to existing audio-visual quality assessment remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include the AGAVQA-3k name, localized wording edits, affiliation/publication information, an Impact Statement, and reorganized appendices separating human evaluation from dataset construction and experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds the scoring-interface figure and compact backbone, rating-variability, and category-accuracy tables. Table 3 gains rows and training-status headings; Tables 1–2 and Figure 2 receive label corrections. Existing MOS plots and instruction/latency tables are retained and relocated, with the overall visual format preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps by reporting rating reliability and comparing selection against fine-tuned baselines, while substantially improving annotation and preprocessing documentation. Corrected metric headers also resolve inconsistencies between v1's benchmark and ablation tables. These gains strengthen the paper's evidential support and reproducibility despite conflicting scoring ranges, the pretraining-count mismatch, and the unsupported interpretation of correlation as independence.
